blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Find the global and local extrema of \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\) over \([-1, 2]\). (Hint: Use the increasing and decreasing behavior of the functions including the end points.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh sawal global aur local dono extrema maangta hai, aur hint kehta hai ke end points ko bhi shamil karna hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\), closed interval \([-1, 2]\) par.
Rule: andar ke points ke liye \(f'\) ke sign ki tabdeeli; end point par yeh dekhna ke function us se door jate hue barhta hai ya ghatta hai (Figure 2.5 ke \(a\) aur \(b\) ki tarah).
Plan: sign table, values, phir local extrema, phir muqabla kar ke global.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\), \(x \in [-1, 2]\).
Maloom karna: tamaam local extrema aur global extrema.
Tareeqa: increasing/decreasing ka rawaiya (2.9.2) aur values (2.10.3). End point se andar ki taraf function gire to woh local maximum, uthe to local minimum.

Critical point
\[f'(x) = -2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0 \in [-1, 2]\]
Kyun: \(f'\) har jagah exist karta hai, is liye sirf yahi critical point hai, aur yeh interval ke andar hai.

\(f'\) ka sign
\[f'\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1 > 0 \text{ on } (-1, 0)\]
\[f'(1) = -2 < 0 \text{ on } (0, 2)\]
Kyun: yani \([-1, 0]\) par increasing aur \([0, 2]\) par decreasing.

Values
\[f(-1) = 3,\quad f(0) = 4,\quad f(2) = 0\]
Kyun: critical point aur dono end points ki values.

Local extrema
\(x = 0\): pehle charhai phir utraai: local maximum \(f(0) = 4\).
\(x = -1\) (left end): is ke baad function barhta hai, yani yeh apne qareebi points se neecha hai: local minimum \(f(-1) = 3\).
\(x = 2\) (right end): function yahan tak girta hua aata hai: local minimum \(f(2) = 0\).
Kyun: 2.10.2 ki definition \(I \cap I_{1}\) use karti hai, yani end point ka muqabla sirf interval ke andar wale qareebi points se hota hai.
Dhyan dein: \(f(-1) = 3\) local minimum hai halan ke yeh sab se chhoti value nahin; local ka matlab sirf "apne aas paas".

Global extrema
3, 4, 0 ka muqabla: global maximum 4, global minimum 0.
Kyun: 2.10.3 ka teesra step. Yahan \(x = 0\) wala local maximum hi global maximum bhi hai, aur \(x = 2\) wala local minimum hi global minimum; jab ke \(x = -1\) wala local minimum sirf local hai, global nahin.
Tasdeeq: \(4 - x^{2} \le 4\) hamesha. Aur \([-1, 2]\) par sab se bara \(x^{2}\) to \(2^{2} = 4\) hai, jis se sab se chhoti value 0 milti hai. Dono baatein hamare jawab se milti hain.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum \(f(0) = 4\) (yahi global maximum bhi hai); local minima \(f(-1) = 3\) aur \(f(2) = 0\); global minimum \(f(2) = 0\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Find the global and local extrema of \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\) over \([0, 2\pi]\). (Hint: Use the increasing and decreasing behavior of the functions including the end points.)
blocks.explanation:
Global aur local extrema ka sawal, trigonometric function ke saath, end points samet.
Diya: \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\), interval \([0, 2\pi]\).
Rule: sign table se andar ke extrema, end points par function ka rukh, aur values ka muqabla.
Plan: \(\tan x = -1\) se critical points, teen tukron ka sign, chaar values, phir faisla.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Maloom karna: tamaam local extrema aur global extrema.
Tareeqa: part (i) wala hi: increasing/decreasing ka rawaiya aur values.

Critical points
\[f'(x) = -\sin x - \cos x = 0\]
\[\tan x = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\sin x = -\cos x\), dono taraf \(\cos x\) se divide. \(\tan\) doosre aur chauthe quadrant mein negative hai: \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\) aur \(2\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\).

\(f'\) ka sign
\[f'\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1 < 0 \text{ on } \left(0, \tfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[f'(\pi) = 1 > 0 \text{ on } \left(\tfrac{3\pi}{4}, \tfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[f'\left(\tfrac{11\pi}{6}\right) = \tfrac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{2} < 0 \text{ on } \left(\tfrac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\right)\]
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{11\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\), \(\cos\frac{11\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), to \(f' = -\left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\), jo negative hai kyun ke \(\sqrt{3} > 1\).

Values
\[f(0) = 1,\quad f\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = -\sqrt{2}\]
\[f\left(\tfrac{7\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2},\quad f(2\pi) = 1\]
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{3\pi}{4} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\sin\frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), to \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = -\sqrt{2}\); isi tarah \(\frac{7\pi}{4}\) par \(\sqrt{2}\).

Local extrema
\(x = 0\) (left end): is ke baad function girta hai: local maximum \(f(0) = 1\).
\(x = \frac{3\pi}{4}\): pehle utraai phir charhai: local minimum \(-\sqrt{2}\).
\(x = \frac{7\pi}{4}\): pehle charhai phir utraai: local maximum \(\sqrt{2}\).
\(x = 2\pi\) (right end): function yahan tak girta hua aata hai: local minimum \(f(2\pi) = 1\).
Kyun: sign table se, end points samet.
Dhyan dein: dono end points ki value 1 hai, phir bhi ek local maximum hai aur doosra local minimum. Faisla value se nahin, function ke rukh se hota hai.

Global extrema
\(1, -\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}, 1\) ka muqabla: global maximum \(\sqrt{2}\), global minimum \(-\sqrt{2}\).
Kyun: 2.10.3.
Tasdeeq: \(\cos x - \sin x = \sqrt{2}\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\), jo hamesha \(-\sqrt{2}\) aur \(\sqrt{2}\) ke darmiyan rehta hai.
blocks.final_answer: Local maxima \(f(0) = 1\) aur \(f\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}\); local minima \(f\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = -\sqrt{2}\) aur \(f(2\pi) = 1\). Global maximum value \(\sqrt{2}\), \(x = \frac{7\pi}{4}\) par; global minimum value \(-\sqrt{2}\), \(x = \frac{3\pi}{4}\) par.
